summary: Locked model diversion during gradual traffic shift with sticky-sessions
description: Issue summary: During a staged traffic shift (20% -> 50%) for customer Numi Insights, a subset of ongoing sessions that were previously pinned to model redwood-open-7b-v2.1 were unexpectedly routed to rwd-chat-3b-codex for several minutes. Impact: ~4% of requests from the tenant received responses from the wrong model variant, causing subtle answer-format regressions in production. Environment: dedicated pool in prod-us-west-2; canary weight change initiated by customer via Console UI at 2026-03-10T12:05Z. Steps to reproduce: 1) Customer pins tenant to redwood-open-7b-v2.1. 2) Start a multistep chat session (long-lived stream, tokenized prefix). 3) Incremental canary weight increase from 20% to 50% via Console. 4) Observe session affinity and model selection logs. Observed behavior: some sessions with active KV-cache and sticky cookies switched variants midstream and responses showed tokenization mismatch. Expected behavior: pinned sessions should retain model affinity until explicit unpin or session TTL expiry. Temporary workaround applied: support cleared route cache on affected edge nodes, forced affinity refresh and rolled back canary weight to 20% while SRE investigates.

2026-03-10T12:35Z - SRE (Marcus Lee): Reproduced mixed responses in staging by simulating long-poll sessions + gradual weight increase. Logged request IDs and attached edge-proxy traces to ticket.
2026-03-10T12:50Z - Customer (Elena R., Numi Insights): Confirmed rollback to 20% restored expected outputs; they need guidance on safe rollout for long-lived sessions.

2026-03-11T09:05Z - Runtime Eng (Sophie Zhang): Noted a coordinator commit that changes delayed pin-commit behavior could interact with TTL-based affinity. Opening PR to add logging and guardrails (see related PR).

investigation_notes: Timeline: canary increase initiated at 12:05Z; first mixed-model responses observed at ~12:07Z; peaked at 12:12Z; rollback started 12:18Z.

Hypothesis 1: session-affinity token rotation race with canary-coordinator commit. Long-lived sessions using prefix/KV cache were re-associated due to an edge-proxy rebind that occurred when routing tables updated midstream.

Hypothesis 2: coordinator applied a partial commit that updated candidate variant sets without atomically swapping affinity pointers, allowing a short window where affinity lookup returned the new candidate but session pin pointer still referenced old instance metadata leading to misrouting to compatible-but-different model.

Logs: trace IDs rwd-req-78a2.. show affinity lookup returned "variant=B" while session-cookie mapped to "variant=A". Edge logs show TTL extension requests at the same second as routing table refreshes.
Staging repro: simulated delayed canary commit with token-rotation reproduced a 2.1% diversion in controlled test; disabling async affinity refresh removed the divergence.

Potential contributing factor: recent coordinator optimization for non-blocking commit introduced an early index refresh; this reduces latency but may create transient lookup inconsistency under in-flight session renewals.
Customer workload note: Numi has a high proportion of long-lived chat sessions and uses a custom client that aggressively renews session cookies every 30s.

Immediate mitigation considered: 1) Add a short global gating window where affinity lookups consult both pre- and post-commit mappings for active sessions; 2) Delay route index refresh until session-lease updates are acknowledged.
resolution: Mitigation applied: rolled back canary to 20%, cleared edge route caches and forced session affinity refresh for Numi Insights, which reduced wrong-variant responses to under 0.5%. Deployed a coordinator-staging patch (PR #1987) that makes commit-to-index refresh atomic for affinity pointers; patch is in canary-staging and under load test. Next steps: 1) Promote patch to prod in a controlled window with extra observability for session divergence metrics. 2) Add a Console warning when a rollout is attempted for tenants with >10% long-lived sessions; recommend slower weight ramps and prewarm. 3) Follow up with customer on client cookie-renewal cadence to reduce edge churn. The ticket remains open until prod promotion and customer acceptance complete.
